author: Neklat
quote: Grand Theft Auto, or Grand Relationship Simulator?Rating: 0/10I bought Grand Theft Auto VI expecting what made this franchise legendary: criminal freedom, chaos, dark humour, outrageous activities, unrestricted exploration and the ability to live out a criminal fantasy in an open world.Instead, I feel like I’m playing a heavily restricted relationship simulator disguised as Grand Theft **** biggest disappointment is the lack of player freedom. Jason is supposed to be a criminal, someone who steals cars, commits robberies and kills people, yet the game seems determined to restrict his personal choices and make him an accommodating partner to Lucia. The relationship mechanics are particularly frustrating. Ordinary domestic activities become mandatory, and refusing to comply can negatively affect the relationship. There are moments when you cannot even pursue another activity because Lucia demands your attention. Why give players an open world if their freedom is constantly subordinated to scripted relationship obligations?The double standards in the relationship are also disappointing. Jason feels increasingly like a supporting character in Lucia’s story rather than an independent protagonist with his own personality, boundaries and desires. A committed relationship is perfectly reasonable as a narrative choice, but forcing the player into a particular relationship dynamic is another matter **** adult content is another disappointment. Previous GTA games offered a degree of freedom in their adult interactions that helped define the franchise’s irreverent identity. Male performers appear in the game, yet I haven’t found a way to request a private dance from one while playing as Jason. The absence of meaningful choices in this area feels particularly inconsistent with the franchise’s traditional sandbox approach.Then there is the vehicle system. This is Grand Theft Auto, yet stealing a car and keeping it involves additional registration and ownership mechanics. I don’t want to pay for a car I’ve already stolen! Vehicle theft should be an organic part of the experience, not another administrative exercise.I am also concerned about the direction of Rockstar’s monetization strategy. I don’t want to see basic gameplay freedom, activities or meaningful advantages withheld from the full-price single-player experience to make a future subscription-based online mode more attractive. That would be an unacceptable approach to consumers, although I acknowledge that the future GTA Online model has not yet been established.I recognize the technical achievements, production values, graphics and attention to detail. However, technical excellence does not automatically translate into an enjoyable Grand Theft Auto experience.I didn’t buy this game to spend my time being Jason’s girlfriend’s ideal boyfriend, managing a relationship, asking permission to enjoy activities or paying to retain stolen property.I bought Grand Theft Auto because I wanted to be a criminal in an open-world **** far, that is precisely what I feel this game has forgotten.Rockstar, I wanted Grand Theft Auto. Not Grand Relationship Simulator.
